existing_observations.text: In the ground phrases 'for this reason' and 'the reason why' (G1223, G5124, G5484, G1352, G0156) the member names the ground on which an act or state stands: Paul's sending to learn of faith (1Th 3:5), the comfort he received (1Th 3:7), the mercy received (1Ti 1:16), his imprisonment and prayer (Eph 3:1, Eph 3:14), his hindering (Rom 15:22), the chain he wears (Act 28:20) and the reminder to Timothy (2Ti 1:6). In each the ground is stated first and what rests on it follows, 8 to 13 words later where the stored positions are given.

Reasoning is a done act of speech in seven Acts verses: Paul reasons in the synagogue, in the marketplace, in the hall of Tyrannus and before Felix (Act 17:2, 17:17, 18:4, 18:19, 19:8, 19:9, 24:25). The verb stands in the aorist or imperfect and is spoken to hearers, with persuading beside it in several; it is an exchange of grounds in speech and not a silent act.

The ground is set beside bearing and sin in four verses: sin is not borne by reason of the offering (Num 18:32), Paul could bear it no longer and sent (1Th 3:5), the sins are what the reasoning together addresses (Isa 1:18), and the Son of God appeared on the ground of the devil's sinning (1Jo 3:8). The reasoning or the ground is thus named where a burden or a sin stands within a few words.

Believing meets the reasoning in four verses. In Act 19:9 the unbelief is 10 words before Paul's reasoning, as what the reasoning meets; in 1Th 3:5, 1Th 3:7 and 1Ti 1:16 faith or believing is 8 to 13 words after the phrase 'for this reason', as what the ground leads to. The reasoning answers unbelief, and the stated ground is followed by faith.

Sin meets the ground and the reasoning in three verses: sin is 1 word before the reason in Num 18:32 (no sin borne by reason of the offering), 4 after the reasoning together in Isa 1:18, and 3 and 9 before the ground in 1Jo 3:8 (the devil sinning from the beginning). Sin is the matter the reasoning addresses or the ground that is stated.

The ground is denied in four verses: 'for no reason' (Job 1:9, Pro 3:30), no reason for the death penalty (Act 28:18) and the question whether this is not the reason (Mar 12:24). The negator reaches the reason itself in the first three, so the ground is stated as absent; in Mar 12:24 the question puts it as the answer.

Reasoning and the ground run in different directions across the verses: from Paul to hearers in the Acts verses, from Jesus to those he answers in Mar 12:24, from the Lord to the people in Isa 1:18, and from God to Paul in 1Ti 1:16, where mercy is received for this reason. God and Jesus are named more often than any human in these verses, and Paul, who reasons in the Acts verses, is not among the stored entities.

Three words in the units of 'reason' do not carry the sense of the group: the copula H1961 in Eze 19:10 (flagged in #2533), the function words G2596 and G0302 in Act 18:14 and the adjective G2138 in Jam 3:17 ('open to reason', compliant). They are read as standalone in their verses; the causal phrase 'for this reason', which makes up most of the surface 'reason', is a ground and not a thought, which the double-meaning observation records.

Knowing meets the reasoning and the ground in three verses. In Mar 12:24 the ground of the error is the lack of knowing (2 words after the phrase of reason) and the negator reaches the knowing; in Luk 9:47 Jesus' knowing is 1 word before the reasoning in the disciples' hearts; in 1Th 3:5 learning is 6 after the ground. Knowing is the ground or the knower of the reasoning.

What the reasoning is on, where the verses give it, is the Scriptures in Act 17:2, the topics of righteousness, self-control and judgment before Felix in Act 24:25 and the kingdom of God in Act 19:8; the objects are matters of teaching put to hearers, with persuading as the aim in Act 18:4, 19:8.

Bearing meets the ground in three verses: 'bear' is 2 words before the ground in Num 18:32 (bear no sin by reason of it) and 2 after in 1Th 3:5 (could bear it no longer), and 'patience' is 9 after in 1Ti 1:16. The ground is stated in the same clause as the bearing in the first two.

Where the ground is denied (Job 1:9, Pro 3:30, Act 28:18) the act is a refusal of a ground: Satan asks whether Job fears God for nothing, the proverb forbids contending without cause, and the Romans found no ground for the penalty.

Words of duration stand 7 to 17 words from the reasoning or the ground in three verses (Dan 4:34, 1Ti 1:16, 1Pe 3:15), in other clauses and phrases (the everlasting kingdom, eternal life, always being prepared). The two meet only in that the verse says something is lasting beside the ground; no tie of grammar joins them.

Knowing is stated as the ground of error in Mar 12:24: the ground of the error is a lack of knowledge, of the Scriptures and of God's power, and the negator reaches the knowing. In Luk 9:47 the knowing is Jesus' knowing of the disciples' reasoning. The ground and the knowing stand within two words of each other in both verses.

Two qualifiers give the reasoning its manner and length: 'three' Sabbath days in Act 17:2 (2 words before) gives how long it went on, and 'like a child' in 1Cor 13:11 (1 before and 2 after) gives the kind of reckoning. The qualifier of the ground in Rom 15:22 is 'often', which gives the repeated hindering the reason accounts for.

*dialogizomai / dialogismos* | Honest troubled reasoning · hardened anxious reasoning · inner questioning seen by Jesus · reasoning together into murder · self-talk of the rich man · quarrel, dispute, opinions · argument about greatness · futile thinking · evil thoughts from the heart · partiality: "judges with evil thoughts" · thoughts revealed by the child set for a sign | Luk 1:29 · Mar 8:16–17; Mat 16:7–8 · Mar 2:6, 8; Luk 5:21–22; 6:8; 9:47 · Luk 20:14; Mat 21:25 · Luk 12:17 · 1Ti 2:8 ("without anger or quarreling"); Phili 2:14; Rom 14:1 · Luk 9:46 · Rom 1:21; 1Co 3:20 · Mar 7:21; Mat 15:19 · Jam 2:4 · Luk 2:35 | Inner reasoning becomes outward quarrel when it is shared and set on one's own standing (Luk 9:46; Rom 14:1) (R). The heart state decides honest or hardened (Luk 1:29 against Mar 8:17, S). In 1Ti 2:8 the quarrel word stands beside anger, a link to the anger strand

In Luk 9:47 the reasoning is inward: it is in the hearts of the disciples after their dispute, and it is Jesus who knows it, the knowing standing 1 word before the member. The same noun therefore gives an unspoken reasoning here and the spoken reasoning of the Acts verses.
In 1Cor 13:11 the reckoning is the working out of a child and is set among speaking and thinking as one of the ways of a child; the verb is a past tense and is given up when the speaker became a man.

to_trace.text: Reasoning as argument put to other people: Paul reasons with Jews and others in the synagogue, the market and the hall of Tyrannus and before Felix, and the Lord invites the people to argue the case out together. The word is spoken argument with a hearer and a matter, aimed at persuading or setting right; the Greek verb is of discourse and the Hebrew verb of arguing a case. Verses: Act 17:2, Act 17:17, Act 18:4, Act 18:19, Act 24:25, Act 19:8, Act 19:9, Isa 1:18.

Reasoning inside the mind: the reckoning of a child in 1Cor 13:11, a way of working things out that is given up in adulthood, and the reasoning in the hearts of the disciples in Luk 9:47, which Jesus knows. Both are reasoning held within a person, not argued to another. Verses: Luk 9:47, 1Cor 13:11.

Reason as understanding, the sound mind: in Dan 4 the king's reason is lost in his madness and returns to him when he lifts his eyes to heaven. The word names the faculty itself. Verses: Dan 4:34, Dan 4:36.

Reason as the ground or cause of something: the cause of a coming, the ground of a charge, 'for this reason' and 'by reason of' as links to what an act or a state rests on, and the reason an act was done or a person appeared. The words are nouns and linking phrases of cause, in many Hebrew and Greek words, and carry no act of thinking. Verses: Gen 41:31, Gen 47:13, Num 18:32, Jos 5:4, 1Sa 20:29, 1Ki 11:27, Eze 19:10, Mar 12:24, Act 10:21, Act 18:14, Act 28:18, Act 28:20, Rom 15:22, Eph 3:1, Eph 3:14, 1Th 3:5, 1Th 3:7, 1Ti 1:16, 2Ti 1:6, 1Jo 3:8.

Reason denied: 'for no reason' is the Hebrew adverb of without cause, said of fearing God for nothing and of contending with a man who has done no harm. It is the absence of a ground. Verses: Job 1:9, Pro 3:30.
Reason as readiness to be persuaded: the wisdom from above is 'open to reason', a trait of the person who yields to others. It is a character trait of the one reasoned with. Verses: Jam 3:17.

Reason as an account given: the believer is to be ready to give a reason to anyone who asks, an explanation of the hope that is in him. It is a spoken account in answer to a question. Verses: 1Pe 3:15.

senses.obs_text: The codes of this sense are G1256 (to dispute, 7), H3198 (to rebuke, 1). The Greek G1256 is the verb of discourse and argument and the Hebrew H3198 is of arguing a case, which agree with reasoning put to other people. The lexicon entry of the main code G1256 gives: to reason, discuss, discourse; to argue, dispute. Verses: Isa 1:18, Act 19:8, Act 24:25, Act 19:9, Act 17:17, Act 17:2, Act 18:4, Act 18:19.

The codes of this sense are G1261 (reasoning, 1), G3049 (to count, 1). G3049 is the verb of reckoning and G1261 the noun of reasoning and thought, which agree with reasoning held within a person. The lexicon entry of the main code G1261 gives: thought, doubt; argument, dispute. Verses: Luk 9:47, 1Cor 13:11.

The codes of this sense are H4486 (knowledge, 2). H4486 is knowledge and the power of knowing, which agrees with reason as the sound mind. The lexicon entry of the main code H4486 gives: knowledge, power of knowing. Verses: Dan 4:36, Dan 4:34.

The codes of this sense are G1223 (through/because of, 4), G0156 (cause/charge, 4), G5124 (that, 3), H6440I (face: because, 2), H5921A (upon, 2), H1697M (word: because, 2), G5484 (because of, 2), H3651C (so, 1), H1961 (to be, 1), G2596 (according to, 1), G0302 (if, 1), G1352 (therefore, 1), G1519 (toward, 1). The codes are prepositions, conjunctions, adverbs and nouns of cause (G0156 cause, G1352 therefore, G5484 for this reason, H5921A on account of); they agree with a ground, and none names an act of thinking. The lexicon entry of the main code G1223 gives: (genitive) through, by means of; (accusitive) because of, for the sake of, therefore genitive., through, used of place or medium, Mt. 7:13; . Verses: Gen 41:31, Gen 47:13, Num 18:32, Jos 5:4, 1Sa 20:29, 1Ki 11:27, Eze 19:10, Mar 12:24, Act 10:21, Act 18:14, Act 28:20, Act 28:18, Rom 15:22, Eph 3:1, Eph 3:14, 1Th 3:7, 1Th 3:5, 1Ti 1:16, 2Ti 1:6, 1Jo 3:8.

The codes of this sense are H2600 (for nothing, 2). H2600 is for nothing or without cause, which agrees with the denial of a ground. The lexicon entry of the main code H2600 gives: freely, for nothing, without cause. Verses: Job 1:9, Pro 3:30.

The codes of this sense are G2138 (compliant, 1). G2138 is easily persuaded and compliant, which agrees with readiness to be persuaded. The lexicon entry of the main code G2138 gives: submissive, obedient, compliant. Verses: Jam 3:17.

The codes of this sense are G3056 (word, 1). G3056 is a word or thing uttered, which agrees with an account given. The lexicon entry of the main code G3056 gives: word, spoken or written, often with a focus on the content of a communication (note the many contextual translations in NIV); matter, thing.. Verses: 1Pe 3:15.
